questions.text: I resist pecking orders and advocate for egalitarian group dynamics.
I tend not to notice when someone shifts their gaze away to signal they are done with a topic.
I experience a new environment as a barrage of stimulation that takes time to process.
I generally negotiate the terms of a collaboration with all parties.
When a stranger is in visible distress, I feel little wish to help.
I often wish I could do something for people who are having a hard time.
I feel a surge of energy when a team collectively discovers its new direction.
I don't tend to carry the emotional residue of one event into the next.
I sense the social temperature of an email based on word choice, punctuation, and formatting.
Reflecting on someone's difficulties rarely makes me feel any wish to ease them.
When I think through someone's problem, I care about the pain it is causing them.
I pick up on when someone deliberately mentions a deadline or constraint to create urgency and shift the power balance.
Learning that people are suffering somewhere else seldom makes me care what happens to them.
I detect when a joke lands differently than the speaker intended.
I respond to messages when the timing feels right, not according to a self-imposed schedule.
I would choose a lower-paying role that lets me serve my community over a higher-paying one that does not.
I practice important skills repeatedly until they become second nature.
I tend to feel the full weight of an experience rather than experiencing it at a distance.
I feel a strong wish to help when someone I know is struggling.
I tend to choose the harder path if it clears the way for someone else.
I tend to structure group decisions around outcomes that benefit me most.
I am quick to assert my expertise when a topic I know well comes up.
When there is a vacuum of leadership, I fill it without thinking twice.
I trust my own judgment more than the group's consensus.
I find deep satisfaction in checking items off a well-organized to-do list.
I invest time creating systems that make future work easier even if setup takes a while.
I do not usually notice when someone edits their story in real time based on audience reactions.
I tend to use unexpected free time for personal projects rather than reaching out to see if someone needs help.
I hold the view that personal ambition and drive are qualities to be proud of, not downplayed.
My baseline emotional state is one of calm readiness.
I notice that music, films, and stories move me intellectually more than they move me physically.
I deal with maintenance needs when they become apparent rather than on a schedule.
I routinely adjust my pace, my route, or my method to match what works best for others.
I let Monday morning unfold and see what the week brings.
When my expectations are violated, my system reacts as if to a physical shock.
I tend to miss when a person's enthusiasm about a topic is meant to signal something about their values.
